title: GBF Eval Result
description: One GBF (Golden-Baseline-File) grading result for a single Wiki Output File (WOF). GBF asks, for the entries the WOF actually contains: is its prose faithful in meaning to the gold, and are its History events in the right chronological order? This is the GBF instance of a shared eval envelope (FC uses eval="fc" with a flat summary; the rubric uses eval="rubric" with presence/sourcing sub-scores). GBF reuses the same status vocabulary (pass/partial/fail/na/skipped): a faithfulness item folds per-claim affirmed/contradicted/omitted verdicts into one status (any contradiction -> fail, all affirmed -> pass, some omitted -> partial, entity absent -> na), and those per-claim verdicts live only in the item's evidence text, never as a status. GBF is all-model: every item has engine="model". Emitted files are plain JSON with no comments. The Pydantic v2 models in evals/gbf/models.py + evals/common/models.py are the real contract; this schema mirrors them.

eval.description: Which eval produced this file. Const "gbf" here so the GBF schema validates strictly; fc/rubric are sibling schemas that reuse the $defs below.

schema_version.description: Version of THIS envelope shape (not the gold contents). Bump only when the envelope structure changes.

wof.description: Filename or path of the graded Wiki Output File. The join key that ties the fc/rubric/gbf results for one run together.

graded_at.description: UTC timestamp when this result was produced.

graders.description: Who/what produced the results. GBF is all-model, so this is a single model grader (GBF has no mechanical grader; whether the model actually ran is carried by summary.complete + item skipped status).

items.description: One entry per criterion evaluated. Keyed by stable id: gbf.faithfulness.<gold-entry-slug> (one per gold entry, the universe) + the single gbf.ordering.

engine.description: Which engine judged this. GBF only ever emits "model" (ordering rests on the model-produced pairing).

status.description: Result for one criterion. pass/fail as expected. partial = partially met (faithfulness: some gold claims omitted, none contradicted; ordering: a small number of inversions); SCORES as a fail but kept visible. na = criterion does not apply to this WOF (faithfulness: the gold entry is absent from the WOF; ordering: fewer than 2 rankable events present); excluded from the denominator. skipped = not evaluated this run (the model was disabled/unavailable, or a check degraded); excluded from the denominator AND flips summary.complete to false.

evidence.description: Why the status was assigned. Required on every item.

lines.description: Line number(s) in the WOF the finding refers to. Empty for whole-document checks.

detail.description: A one-line rationale. Faithfulness names the contradicted/omitted gold claims and appends any WOF-only claims as [EXTRA] notes (orthogonal to the status). Ordering names the out-of-order pairs.

found.description: Optional. What was actually present (e.g. a supporting WOF span).

id.description: Stable criterion id (dotted gbf.* slug). The ONLY join key; results reference the id, never the prose. Faithfulness tokens embed gold-entry slugs which may contain non-ASCII letters, so the pattern allows any non-dot, non-whitespace token.

description.description: Informational copy of the criterion text. NOT authoritative; the id wins. Safe to omit.

subscore.description: One bucket's applicable-only tally. No complete/skipped here — those are run-level on the summary.

partial.description: Counts toward fail in scoring; surfaced separately.

applicable.description: pass + partial + fail. The denominator (na and skipped excluded).

score.description: pass / applicable, in 0..1. null when applicable == 0.

summary.description: Two independent sub-scores under a run-level complete. There is no combined top score. items[] is the source of truth.

complete.description: false when any item was skipped (the model was off/unavailable, or a check degraded). Makes a provisional grade visibly provisional.

grader.description: A mechanical grader or a model grader, discriminated on engine. GBF only emits a model grader.
